newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia orders firms to give profits to poor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia orders firms to give profits to poor.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto, in a decree released on Friday, has ordered companies with an annual after-tax profit of 100 million rupiah and above to contribute two percent of their after-tax profit to the poor.

"Individuals and companies have to give two percent of their after-tax profit to poor families in one tax year," said the decree, dated December 4 and effective in the 1996 tax year, released by the State Secretariat.
In September Suharto asked Indonesia's wealthy why they had ignored a government appeal in 1995 to donate two percent of their profits to alleviate poverty.

The 1995 appeal for donations to the government's poverty alleviation programme was issued in the form of a presidential decree and addressed to private companies and individuals with an after-tax income of more than 100 million rupiah a year.
The December 4 order changed the words in section two of the 1995 decree to say that companies and individuals "must give" to the poor, instead of "can help" the poor.
